text:
Alex Killorn is 37, has two Stanley Cups from Tampa and more than 1,000 NHL games, and he's still playing 16 minutes a night for a Ducks team that has started winning. The points have dried up, though: six straight games without one, and five points in 17.

Part of that is bad fortune. Anaheim has scored 4.6 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and his own shooting is under his usual range. He's also 7.5 points better than his teammates in 5v5 expected goals share, which says he's still helping.

Part of it is age. His chances have thinned in the pointless run, and NHL EDGE has his top speed in the 9th percentile. Our comparisons put him alongside Sean Couturier and Anton Lundell: penalty killers who get matched against good players. That's his job now, and on a young team the experience matters even when the scoresheet doesn't show it. Our range has him around 32 points.
headline: Killorn at 37, still in the middle of it
